## Our Plumbing Services in Burien, WA

We handle the plumbing jobs Burien homeowners call about most: emergency repairs, clogged drains, water heater repair and replacement, hidden leaks, sewer line problems, and broken or worn-out pipes. Each one has its own page with prices, warning signs, and what to expect.

### Emergency Plumber

Burst pipe, overflowing toilet, or sewage coming up a floor drain? Call our 24/7 emergency plumber line. We talk you through shutting off the water while a plumber heads your way, then stop the leak, protect your home, and give you a firm price before any repair starts.

### Drain Cleaning

Slow sink, clogged toilet, or a main line backing up into the tub? Our drain cleaning service clears kitchen, bath, and sewer lines with snakes and hydro jetting. If the clog keeps coming back, we run a camera to find the cause, so you pay to fix it once, not every few months.

### Water Heater Repair

No hot water, a leaking tank, or rusty water from the tap? We repair and replace gas, electric, and tankless water heaters across Burien. Most repairs are done in one visit. If your tank is near the end of its life, you get clear repair and replace prices before we start.

### Leak Detection

High water bill, a damp ceiling, or the sound of running water when everything is off? Our leak detection service uses listening gear, moisture meters, and thermal cameras to find hidden leaks in walls, slabs, and yard lines, so we open only what we must and fix it fast.

### Sewer Line Repair

Sewage smells, gurgling drains, or backups in more than one fixture? Many Burien homes still have old clay side sewers that crack and fill with roots. We camera-inspect the line, show you the video, and quote root removal, spot repair, or trenchless replacement up front.

### Pipe Repair & Repiping

Burst, frozen, or leaking pipes, low pressure, or brown water from old galvanized lines? We fix single pipe sections the same day when possible and repipe whole homes in PEX or copper. You get a written price first, and we patch the access holes we make when the job is done.

Not sure which one fits your problem? That is fine. Call and describe what you see, hear, or smell. We will tell you what it most likely is and what it usually costs before anyone drives out.

## Which plumbing repair do you need? Check your symptoms

Pick the symptom that matches what you see. Each one links to the service that usually fixes it, with prices and warning signs. If you notice more than one, start with the most urgent and call. We can sort it out together on the phone.

- Water spraying or coming through the ceiling Urgent Emergency Plumber
- No hot water or a puddle under the tank Urgent Water Heater Repair
- Sewage smell or backup in a floor drain Urgent Sewer Line Repair
- Pipes froze during a cold snap Urgent Pipe Repair & Repiping

- Water bill jumped with no new use Soon Leak Detection
- One sink, tub, or toilet slow to drain Schedule Drain Cleaning

Pro tip

Find your main water shutoff today, before you need it. In most Burien homes it is in the crawl space, basement, or garage. Tag it so anyone in the house can find it fast.

## Do you need a 24 hour emergency plumber right now?

It is an emergency if water is spreading, sewage is backing up, you smell gas, or you have no water or no heat source for hot water in winter. Those problems get worse every hour. Call right away, even at night. Slow drips and running toilets can usually wait for a scheduled visit.

### Call now for these

- A burst or spraying pipe
- Water coming through a ceiling or wall
- Sewage coming up in a tub, shower, or floor drain
- A leaking water heater, or no hot water at all
- A toilet that overflows and will not stop
- Frozen pipes during a cold snap

### What to do while you wait

- Shut off the main water valve. In most Burien homes it is in the crawl space, basement, or garage, near where the line enters the house. Some homes also have a shutoff at the meter box near the street.
- For a leaking water heater, turn the cold water valve on top to off. On gas units, turn the gas knob to "pilot" or "off." On electric units, switch off the breaker.
- Stop using sinks, toilets, and the washer if drains are backing up.
- Move rugs, boxes, and electronics away from the water. Take photos for insurance.

### What changes the price

- Access. A pipe behind finished drywall or under a slab takes more time than one in an open crawl space.
- Time of day. Nights, weekends, and holidays cost more.
- Parts. A 50-gallon gas water heater costs more than a 40-gallon electric one.
- Permits. Water heater swaps and sewer work often need a permit from the City of Burien or King County.

## What plumbing repairs do Burien homes need most?

Burien homes face three big issues: aging pipes from the 1940s to 1970s, tree roots in sewer lines, and wet winters that push groundwater and debris into drains. Our water is soft, so mineral scale is rarely the problem. Old pipe material and roots usually are.

### Older pipe materials

Many homes in Burien and nearby White Center and Boulevard Park still have galvanized steel water lines. Galvanized pipe rusts from the inside. Over time you get low water pressure, brown water, and pinhole leaks. Drain lines in these homes are often cast iron, which can crack, and the sewer line out to the street is often clay.

### Tree roots

Burien has a big tree canopy, from Seahurst Park to Lake Burien and Gregory Heights. Roots find tiny gaps in clay sewer joints and grow inside the pipe. The result is a slow main drain that keeps coming back, and sometimes a full backup.

### Rain and cold snaps

Western Washington gets most of its rain from fall to spring. Heavy storms load gutters, yard drains, and sump pumps. Every few years, arctic air drops temperatures into the teens. Pipes in crawl spaces, garages, and outside walls can freeze and split.

### Soft water

Most Burien homes get water from local districts like Highline Water District, which buys supply from Seattle. Published data puts Burien's hardness around 1 to 2 grains per gallon, which is soft. That is easy on water heaters, so tank failures here are more about age than scale.

## Should you fix it yourself or hire a plumber?

You can fix small things yourself, like a running toilet flapper, a clogged sink trap, or a loose faucet handle. Call a plumber for anything that involves gas, sewer lines, water heaters, hidden leaks, or a clog that comes back. Those jobs can cause damage or safety risks if done wrong.

| Problem | DIY is fine | Call a plumber |
| Running toilet | Replace flapper or fill valve | If it still runs or leaks at the base |
| Slow bathroom sink | Clean the stopper and trap | If more than one drain is slow |
| Dripping faucet | Replace a cartridge | If the valve or supply line is corroded |
| No hot water | Check breaker or pilot light | If it leaks, smells like gas, or will not relight |
| Sewer smell | Pour water in unused drains | If the smell stays or drains gurgle |

One rule saves a lot of money: do not use chemical drain cleaner on a main line clog. It rarely reaches the blockage, it can harm older pipes, and it makes the job less safe for the plumber who clears it.

## Frequently asked questions

Short, direct answers to the questions we hear most on the phone. Do not see yours? Call and ask.

**Q: Do you offer 24 hour plumbing service in Burien? **

Yes. We answer calls 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, including holidays. Night, weekend, and holiday visits cost more than daytime visits, and we tell you the extra fee on the phone before you book.

**Q: How fast can a plumber get to my house? **

It depends on the time of day and how many calls are ahead of you. When you call, we give you a real arrival window. Active leaks and sewer backups go to the front of the line.

**Q: Do you give free quotes? **

Yes. We give a free price range on the phone. After the plumber looks at the problem in person, you get a firm price before any work starts.

**Q: Where is my main water shutoff valve? **

In most Burien homes the main valve is where the water line enters the house, often in the crawl space, basement, or garage. There is also a valve in the meter box near the street, which may need a meter key.

**Q: Should I repair or replace my water heater? **

If the tank is under 8 years old and the problem is a part like a thermostat, element, or valve, repair usually makes sense. If the tank is over 10 years old or leaking from the tank itself, replacement is the better buy.

**Q: Why does my main drain keep clogging? **

A main drain that keeps clogging usually has roots, a sag, or a crack in the sewer line. A camera inspection shows the cause so you can fix it once instead of paying for repeat cleanings.

**Q: Do you need a permit for plumbing work in Burien? **

Many jobs do, including water heater replacement and sewer line repair. We tell you on the call if your job needs a permit and include it in the quote.

**Q: What should I tell you when I call? **

Tell us what is happening, when it started, whether water is leaking now, and your address or ZIP. If you know the age of your home or water heater, that helps us give a better price range.

## Which repairs do homeowners need most?

Burien homeowners call most for emergencies, clogged drains, water heaters, hidden leaks, sewer line problems, and old pipes. Those six services cover almost every plumbing problem in a typical home. Each service below links to a full page with signs, process, and costs.

### Emergency Plumber

Burst pipes, overflowing toilets, water through the ceiling, and sewage backups do not wait. Our emergency plumbing service runs 24 hours a day. We help you stop the water on the phone, then send a plumber to make the repair. You hear the after-hours fee before you book.

### Drain Cleaning

Slow sinks, gurgling toilets, and tubs that fill with water while you shower all point to a clog. We clear kitchen, bath, laundry, and main sewer drains with cable machines and hydro jetting. If the clog keeps coming back, we run a camera to find out why.

### Water Heater Repair and Replacement

No hot water, rusty water, popping sounds, or a puddle under the tank? We repair gas, electric, and tankless water heaters, and we replace tanks that are past their useful life. We help you pick the right size so you stop running out of hot water.

### Leak Detection

A high water bill, a meter that spins with everything off, or a warm spot on the floor can mean a hidden leak. We find leaks inside walls, under floors, in crawl spaces, and in the yard line with as little cutting as possible.

### Sewer Line Repair

Many Burien sewer lines are old clay pipe with roots in the joints. We inspect with a camera, clear roots, and repair or replace damaged sections. Where it fits, trenchless repair can save your yard, driveway, and landscaping.

### Pipe Repair and Repiping

Galvanized pipe from the 1940s to 1960s rusts from the inside, which causes low pressure and pinhole leaks. We fix burst and frozen pipes, replace bad sections, and repipe whole homes with PEX or copper when patching no longer makes sense.

## How do you choose the right plumbing repair service?

Match what you notice to the most likely cause. One slow drain is usually a local clog. Several slow drains at once point to the main sewer line. Water where it should not be means a leak. If you are unsure, describe it on the phone and we will narrow it down.

| What you notice | Most likely service |
| Water spraying, spreading, or coming through a ceiling | Emergency plumber |
| One sink or tub drains slowly | Drain cleaning |
| Toilets gurgle and floor drain backs up | Sewer line repair |
| No hot water, or water under the tank | Water heater repair |
| Water bill jumped with no new use | Leak detection |
| Low pressure or brown water in an older home | Pipe repair or repiping |

Pro tip

Text photos when we ask on the call. A picture of the water heater label or the leak helps us bring the right parts and finish in one visit.

## What should you ask before you hire a plumber?

Ask for the price before work starts, what is included, whether a permit is needed, and how long the repair should last. Also ask for the contractor registration number so you can check it with Washington L&I. A good plumber answers all of these without hesitation.

- Is there a trip or diagnostic fee? Know it before the truck rolls.
- Will I get a firm price before you start? The answer should be yes.
- Does the job need a permit? Water heaters and sewer lines often do.
- Is this a repair or a replacement, and why? You should understand the choice.
- What is your Washington contractor registration number? You can look it up on the L&I "Verify a Contractor" tool.
- What happens if the problem comes back? Ask what the plumber stands behind.

Warning

Be careful with big quotes that skip the inspection. A sewer or repipe price given without a camera or a look at the pipes is a guess.

## Can you book same-day service?

Yes, most repairs can be done the same day you call, as long as the plumber has the part on the truck. Emergencies get priority day and night. Larger jobs like sewer replacement or repiping are scheduled after the first visit because they need planning and sometimes a permit.

To help us fix it in one visit, tell us as much as you can on the phone. The brand and size of your water heater, the age of the house, and photos of the problem all help the plumber bring the right parts. Same-day service is never promised until we confirm an open window on the call.

## What does a 24 hour emergency plumber in Burien do?

An emergency plumber comes out after hours to stop active water damage and make a safe repair. That includes burst pipes, overflowing fixtures, sewer backups, leaking water heaters, and frozen lines. The goal is to stop the damage first, then fix the cause, often in the same visit.

Most plumbing emergencies in Burien happen at the worst time. A supply line bursts at 2 a.m. A sewer line backs up on Thanksgiving when the house is full. A water heater lets go on a Sunday. Our after hours plumber service exists for those moments. You call, a person answers, and you get help right away.

## What is included in emergency plumbing repair?

Emergency service includes phone help to stop the water, a priority visit, diagnosis, and a repair that makes your home safe and usable again. If a full fix needs parts or a permit, we make a temporary repair so you have water and working drains in the meantime.

- Step-by-step help on the phone to shut off water or gas
- Priority dispatch ahead of non-urgent calls
- Burst and leaking pipe repair
- Toilet overflow and clogged drain clearing
- Main sewer line backup clearing
- Water heater leak shutoff, repair, or replacement
- Frozen pipe thawing and split pipe repair
- Clear notes and photos you can share with your insurance

Pro tip

## When should you call an emergency plumber right away?

You need an emergency plumber now if water is moving where it should not be, sewage is coming up, or you cannot shut the water off. Waiting even a few hours can mean wet drywall, ruined flooring, and mold. If you can stop the water and use one bathroom, it can often wait until morning.

- Water spraying from a pipe, fitting, or supply line
- A wet, sagging, or dripping ceiling
- Sewage or dirty water rising in a tub, shower, or floor drain
- A water heater leaking from the tank
- A shutoff valve that will not close
- No water in the whole house
- Gas smell near a water heater. Leave the house and call your gas utility first.

## What happens when you call our emergency plumber line?

First we help you stop the water on the phone. Then we dispatch a plumber with an arrival window. On site, the plumber finds the cause, explains the options, and gives you a firm price. Once you approve, the repair starts right away.

- You call (833) 710-2588. Tell us what is happening and your address.
- We help you shut it off. Main valve, fixture valve, or water heater valve.
- A plumber is dispatched. You get an arrival window, and a call if anything changes.
- Diagnosis and price. The plumber shows you the problem and gives a firm price.
- Repair and cleanup. We fix it, test it, and clean the work area.

Warning

If water is near outlets, the electrical panel, or appliances, stay out of it. Shut off power at the breaker only if you can reach it from a dry spot.

## Why call an emergency plumber now instead of waiting?

Water damage spreads fast. A half-inch pipe can release hundreds of gallons an hour. Drywall, subfloor, and insulation soak it up, and mold can start within a day or two. Calling now often costs less than the damage you prevent by acting fast.

In Burien, many homes have crawl spaces. Water can pool under the house where you cannot see it. If you hear running water with every tap off, call us. During cold snaps, we also see many calls for frozen pipes in crawl spaces, garages, and outside walls. When those thaw, they leak. Shut off the main and call before the thaw starts.

## Frequently asked questions

Short, direct answers to the questions we hear most on the phone. Do not see yours? Call and ask.

**Q: Is there an emergency plumber near me in Burien open now? **

Yes. Burien Plumbers answers calls 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Call (833) 710-2588 and tell us your address. We give you a real arrival window.

**Q: How do I shut off my water in an emergency? **

Find the main valve where the water line enters your home, often in the crawl space, basement, or garage. Turn it clockwise until it stops. If it will not move, the meter box near the street has a second shutoff.

**Q: Will my homeowners insurance cover a burst pipe? **

Many policies cover sudden water damage from a burst pipe but not slow leaks or the pipe itself. Take photos, keep your plumber invoice, and call your insurer. We can give you notes on the cause.

**Q: Do emergency plumbers charge more on weekends? **

Yes. Nights, weekends, and holidays usually add $100 to $300 to the service fee. We tell you the exact fee on the phone before we book.

**Q: What counts as a plumbing emergency? **

Active leaks, flooding, sewage backups, no water, a leaking water heater, and frozen pipes are emergencies. A dripping faucet or a slow drain in a second bathroom can wait for a regular visit.

**Q: What if I smell gas near my water heater? **

Leave the house, do not use switches, and call your gas utility or 911 from outside. Once the utility says it is safe, call us to repair the water heater or gas line.

## What is professional drain cleaning service in Burien?

Professional drain cleaning removes clogs and buildup from your pipes with tools made for the job. A cable machine, or drain snake, cuts through clogs and roots. Hydro jetting uses high-pressure water to scour the pipe walls. A camera shows what is causing the clog so the fix lasts.

Store-bought drain cleaner can clear a small clog near the drain. It rarely reaches clogs deeper in the line, and it does nothing for roots or broken pipe. In older Burien homes with cast iron and clay pipes, harsh chemicals can also speed up corrosion. Professional cleaning is the safer choice for anything more than a slow sink.

## What is included when you hire drain cleaning?

Drain cleaning includes finding the clog, clearing it with the right tool, and testing that water flows freely. For main line clogs, it can also include a camera inspection so you see the pipe condition. You get advice on how to prevent the clog from returning.

- Kitchen sink and garbage disposal line clearing
- Bathroom sink, tub, and shower drain clearing
- Toilet clog removal and auger work
- Laundry and floor drain clearing
- Main sewer line cleaning through a cleanout
- Root cutting in sewer lines
- Hydro jetting for grease, scale, and roots
- Video camera inspection with a recording you can keep

Pro tip

Run hot water for 30 seconds after using the garbage disposal. It moves food scraps through the line instead of letting them settle.

## What are the signs you need a drain cleaning plumber?

You need drain cleaning when water drains slowly, drains gurgle, or bad smells come up from the pipes. If more than one fixture is slow at the same time, the clog is likely in the main line. That needs a plumber before it turns into a sewage backup.

- Sinks or tubs that take minutes to drain
- Gurgling sounds when a toilet flushes
- Water coming up in the tub when you run the washer
- Sewer smell from drains or the yard
- Water pooling around a floor drain or cleanout
- Clogs that return a few weeks after you clear them

## How does drain snaking and hydro jetting work?

We start by asking which drains are slow and when it started. The plumber then picks the right access point and tool, clears the line, and runs water to confirm full flow. For repeat or main line clogs, we run a camera to find roots, sags, or breaks.

- Diagnose. Find which drains are affected to locate the clog.
- Access. Use a cleanout, trap, or toilet flange to reach the line.
- Clear. Cable machine for most clogs, hydro jetting for grease and roots.
- Test. Run water through every affected fixture.
- Inspect if needed. Camera the main line to show you the cause.

Warning

## Why book same-day drain cleaning before it backs up?

A slow drain is a warning. Once a main line clogs fully, wastewater has only one place to go: up through your lowest drain. Clearing it early is cheaper, cleaner, and can be scheduled in the day instead of as an after-hours emergency.

Burien's tall trees and wet fall season make root clogs common. Roots grow fastest when they find water in a sewer joint, and fall leaves wash into yard drains during storms. If your drains slow down every fall, a camera inspection can tell you if roots are the cause.

## Frequently asked questions

**Q: How often should I have my drains cleaned? **

Most homes only need drain cleaning when a problem shows up. If your sewer line has roots, cleaning every 12 to 18 months can prevent backups until you are ready to repair the pipe.

**Q: Is hydro jetting safe for old pipes? **

Hydro jetting is safe for most pipes in fair condition. For very old clay or cast iron, we camera the line first. If the pipe is cracked or fragile, we use a cable instead.

**Q: Why does my kitchen sink keep clogging? **

Grease, food scraps, and coffee grounds build up inside the pipe. Over time they narrow the line. Hydro jetting removes the buildup. Scraping plates into the trash helps keep it clear.

**Q: Can I use a plunger on a clogged toilet? **

Yes. A flange plunger works on most toilet clogs. If plunging does not work, or other drains are also slow, stop and call. The clog may be in the main line.

**Q: What is a sewer cleanout? **

A cleanout is a capped pipe that gives plumbers direct access to your sewer line. In Burien homes it is often outside near the foundation or in the crawl space.

**Q: Do you clean drains on weekends? **

Yes. We clear drains 7 days a week. Weekend and night visits cost more, and we tell you the fee before booking.

## What does water heater repair in Burien include?

Water heater repair means finding why the unit is not heating or is leaking, then replacing the failed part. Common fixes are thermostats, heating elements, gas valves, thermocouples, igniters, and relief valves. If the tank itself leaks, it cannot be repaired and needs replacement.

- Diagnosis of no hot water, low hot water, or slow recovery
- Electric element and thermostat replacement
- Gas thermocouple, igniter, and gas control valve service
- Temperature and pressure relief valve replacement
- Flushing sediment and checking the anode rod
- Tankless descaling, error code diagnosis, and part repair
- Tank water heater replacement and haul-away
- Seismic strapping and expansion tank install to code

## What are the signs you need water heater repair?

The common signs are no hot water, hot water that runs out fast, rusty water, popping or rumbling sounds, and water around the base. A leak from the tank body means it is failing. A leak from a valve or fitting can usually be repaired.

- No hot water at any tap
- Hot water runs out much faster than it used to
- Rusty or brown hot water only
- Popping, banging, or rumbling while heating
- Water pooling under or around the tank
- Pilot light that will not stay lit
- Tankless unit showing an error code

Pro tip

## Should you repair or replace your water heater?

Repair your water heater if it is under about 8 years old and a single part has failed. Replace it if it is over 10 years old, the tank is leaking, or repairs keep adding up. A new unit is also worth it if you keep running out of hot water.

| Factor | Repair | Replace |
| Age | Under 8 years | Over 10 years |
| Problem | Failed part | Leaking tank |
| Repair cost | Under 30% of new | Over 50% of new |
| Hot water supply | Enough for your family | Runs out often |

Burien's water is soft, around 1 to 2 grains per gallon in published data. That means less mineral scale than many cities, so tanks here often last close to their full rated life. Age, not scale, is usually what ends a tank in Burien. Find the year in the serial number on the label.

## Is tankless water heater installation worth the cost?

A tankless water heater is worth it if you want endless hot water, plan to stay in the home for years, and have the gas line or electrical capacity to support it. It costs more up front than a tank, but it uses less energy and can last close to 20 years.

Soft water helps tankless units here, since scale is the main thing that wears them down in hard-water cities. The tradeoff is install cost. Many older Burien homes need a larger gas line or new venting. We tell you on the visit what your home would need.

# Leak Detection in Burien, WA

## What is professional leak detection service in Burien?

Leak detection is the process of finding water leaks you cannot see. Plumbers use acoustic listening tools, thermal cameras, moisture meters, and pressure tests to pinpoint leaks inside walls, under floors, and in buried water lines. Finding the exact spot means smaller openings and a cheaper repair.

Without leak detection, finding a hidden leak means guessing and opening walls. That is slow and expensive. With the right tools, a plumber can usually narrow the leak to a small area before cutting anything. Then the repair is quick and the patch is small.

## What is included when you hire leak detection?

Leak detection includes checking your water meter, testing the system for pressure loss, and scanning the likely areas with detection tools. You get the location of the leak and a firm price to repair it. Many repairs can be done on the same visit.

- Water meter test to confirm a leak exists
- Pressure testing of the supply system
- Acoustic listening on pipes and slabs
- Thermal imaging of walls, ceilings, and floors
- Moisture readings in drywall and subfloor
- Yard service line leak location
- Toilet, fixture, and irrigation leak checks
- Repair quote for the leak we find

Pro tip

Read your water meter before bed and again in the morning with no water used. If the numbers changed, you have a leak somewhere.

Have a plumbing problem right now?

(833) 710-2588 A real person answers 24/7 and gives you a price range before booking.

## What are the signs you need a leak detection plumber?

The most common sign is a water bill that jumps without any change in use. Others are a meter that moves with every tap off, damp or stained drywall, warped floors, musty smells, and the sound of running water when nothing is on. Mold in one spot often points to a leak behind it.

- Water bill much higher than the same month last year
- Meter dial moving when all water is off
- Stains or bubbling paint on walls or ceilings
- Soft, warped, or cupping floors
- Musty smell or mold in one area
- Sound of running water at night
- Wet soil or green patches in the yard in dry weather

## How can you check for a water leak before you call?

Turn off every faucet, appliance, and irrigation zone. Then look at your water meter. If the dial or low-flow indicator is still moving, you have a leak. Wait an hour and check again to catch slow leaks. Next, add food coloring to toilet tanks to check for silent toilet leaks.

- Turn off all water use in and out of the house.
- Find your meter, usually in a box near the street.
- Watch the small triangle or star dial for 10 minutes.
- Shut the main valve at the house. If the meter still moves, the leak is in the yard line.
- If it stops, the leak is inside the house.

If your meter shows a leak, call us. Tell us the result of the test. It helps us bring the right tools and give a better price range.

Warning

Do not ignore a small ceiling stain. Water travels along framing, so the leak may be bigger and farther away than the stain.

## How does non-invasive leak detection work?

The plumber confirms the leak with a meter and pressure test, then splits the system into sections to narrow it down. Listening tools and thermal cameras pinpoint the spot. Once found, the plumber shows you the location and quotes the repair.

- Confirm. Meter and pressure tests prove there is a leak.
- Isolate. Shut valves to test hot, cold, and yard lines separately.
- Pinpoint. Acoustic and thermal tools find the exact spot.
- Repair. Open a small area and fix the pipe.
- Verify. Retest to make sure the system holds pressure.

## Should you repair the leak or replace the pipe?

Repair the leak if the pipe is in good shape and this is the first leak. Replace the pipe if you have had more than one leak, the pipe is galvanized, or the leak is in an old service line. Repeated pinhole leaks usually mean the whole line is wearing out.

| Situation | Best choice |
| First pinhole in copper | Repair the section |
| Second or third leak in a year | Plan a repipe |
| Leak in galvanized pipe | Replace that run |
| Leaking yard service line, old material | Replace the line |

In Burien, many houses built before 1970 still have galvanized or early copper lines. Leaks in those homes are often a sign that more are coming. See our pipe repair and repiping page for options.

## Why hire leak detection now instead of waiting?

Hidden leaks keep running all day and night. They raise your water bill, rot framing and subfloor, and grow mold. In Burien's damp climate, crawl spaces and walls do not dry out on their own. Finding the leak early keeps a small repair from becoming a big remodel.

## Frequently asked questions

Short, direct answers to the questions we hear most on the phone. Do not see yours? Call and ask.

**Q: How do plumbers find leaks without opening walls? **

They use acoustic tools that hear water escaping, thermal cameras that see cool wet spots, and moisture meters. These narrow the leak to a small area before any opening.

**Q: Will homeowners insurance pay for leak detection? **

Some policies cover the cost to find and access a leak when it causes covered damage. Check with your insurer. We provide notes and photos to help.

**Q: Can a toilet leak raise my water bill? **

Yes. A running or silent toilet leak can waste thousands of gallons a month. Put food coloring in the tank. If color shows in the bowl without flushing, the flapper is leaking.

**Q: Who fixes the leak between the meter and my house? **

In most cases the homeowner owns the line from the meter to the house. Your water district usually owns the meter and the line on the street side.

**Q: How long does leak detection take? **

Most leak detection visits take 1 to 3 hours. Simple leaks can be found in under an hour. Slab and yard leaks can take longer.

**Q: Is a slab leak common in Burien? **

Slab leaks are less common here because many Burien homes have crawl spaces or basements. They do happen in homes built on slabs, and the signs are warm spots on the floor and constant meter movement.

## What is sewer line repair and replacement in Burien?

Sewer line repair fixes the pipe that carries waste from your house to the public sewer main. Common repairs are clearing roots, replacing a broken or sagging section, lining the pipe from inside, or replacing the whole line. A camera inspection decides which one you need.

In most Burien homes, the homeowner owns the side sewer, which runs from the house to the connection at the street. When it fails, it is your repair. The good news is that most problems can be fixed without digging up the whole yard.

## What is included in sewer line repair service?

Sewer service includes a camera inspection, line locating, root and blockage clearing, and a written repair plan with a firm price. If a repair is needed, we handle digging or trenchless work, permits, inspection, and restoring the area we opened.

## What are the signs you need sewer line repair?

The main signs are several drains backing up at once, gurgling toilets, sewage smell indoors or in the yard, and soggy spots or lush green patches over the line. If water rises in a tub or floor drain when you run the washer, the main line is blocked or broken.

- Two or more drains slow at the same time
- Toilets gurgle or bubble when other fixtures drain
- Sewage coming up in the lowest drain
- Sewer smell in the house or yard
- Wet, sunken, or extra-green patches over the line

## Why do Burien sewer lines need repair or replacement?

Many Burien sewer lines are clay or cast iron pipe from the 1940s to 1970s. Clay joints let roots in, and Burien's big trees send roots toward any water source. Cast iron rusts and cracks with age. Ground movement and long runs on sloped lots also cause sags and breaks.

- Roots. Firs, maples, and cedars near the line push into joints.
- Old clay pipe. Short sections with many joints.
- Cast iron corrosion. Scale builds up, then the pipe cracks.
- Slopes. Hillside lots in Seahurst, Three Tree Point, and Normandy Park have long, steep runs.
- Wet soil. Saturated winter ground can shift poorly bedded pipe.

Warning

Root killer products only slow root growth. They do not fix the cracked joints that let roots in.

## What should you avoid to prevent costly sewer repairs?

Avoid grease, wipes, paper towels, and feminine products. Even "flushable" wipes do not break down fast enough and catch on roots in old clay pipe. Grease cools and sticks to pipe walls. Keeping these out of your drains is the cheapest way to make a sewer line last.

- Cooking grease, oil, and fat
- Wipes of any kind, even if labeled flushable
- Paper towels and tissues
- Coffee grounds and eggshells
- Cat litter

## Should you repair or replace your sewer line?

Repair one section if the camera shows a single break, sag, or root entry point and the rest of the pipe is sound. Replace or line the whole run if there are problems at many joints, the pipe is badly corroded, or it is collapsing. A full fix costs more once but ends repeat calls.

| Camera result | Recommendation |
| One cracked joint | Spot repair |
| Roots at 3+ joints | Lining or replacement |
| Belly holding water | Spot repair of the sag |
| Heavy corrosion, cast iron | Lining or replacement |
| Collapsed pipe | Replacement |

## Why call for sewer line repair now?

A failing sewer line gets worse, not better. Each backup risks raw sewage in your home, which is a health hazard and a costly cleanup. Fixing it on your schedule is cheaper than an after-hours emergency, and it lets you plan the work and permits.

## Frequently asked questions

Short, direct answers to the questions we hear most on the phone. Do not see yours? Call and ask.

**Q: Who is responsible for the sewer line in Burien? **

In most cases the homeowner owns and maintains the side sewer from the house to the public main. Your local sewer district can confirm where your responsibility ends.

**Q: What is trenchless sewer repair? **

Trenchless repair fixes the pipe without digging a long trench. Lining puts a new pipe inside the old one. Pipe bursting pulls a new pipe through as it breaks the old one. Both need only small access holes.

**Q: How long does sewer line repair take? **

A spot repair often takes one day. Full replacement or lining usually takes 1 to 3 days, plus time for permits and inspection.

**Q: Can tree roots really break a sewer pipe? **

Roots enter through small gaps at joints. As they grow, they widen cracks and can break or shift the pipe. Clay pipe is the most at risk.

**Q: Should I get a sewer inspection before buying a home in Burien? **

Yes. Many Burien homes have older side sewers. A camera inspection costs a few hundred dollars and can reveal a repair worth thousands before you buy.

**Q: Does homeowners insurance cover sewer line repair? **

Standard policies often do not cover wear, roots, or age. Some insurers offer a service line add-on. Check your policy and ask about sewer backup coverage too.

## What does pipe repair and repiping in Burien include?

Pipe repair includes fixing burst, frozen, cracked, or leaking water lines, and replacing worn-out sections. For homes with failing galvanized or old copper pipe, it can mean a whole-house repipe with PEX or copper. The goal is safe water pressure and no more leaks.

- Burst pipe repair, day or night
- Frozen pipe thawing and split pipe replacement
- Pinhole leak repair in copper
- Galvanized pipe section replacement
- Shutoff valve and supply line replacement
- Whole-house repiping with PEX or copper
- Pipe insulation for crawl spaces and garages
- Water pressure testing and pressure regulator service

## What are the signs you need pipe repair or repiping?

Look for low water pressure, brown or rusty water, repeat pinhole leaks, and visible rust or green buildup on pipes. Homes built before 1970 with galvanized pipe often show all of these. One leak can be repaired. Many leaks mean the pipes are near the end of their life.

- Low pressure at several faucets, worse on hot side
- Brown or rusty water after the tap sits
- More than one leak in a year
- Rust, flaking, or bulges on exposed pipe
- Green or white crust on copper fittings
- Banging or knocking pipes
- Gray metal pipe with threaded joints (galvanized)

Pro tip

Before a cold snap, disconnect garden hoses and close crawl space vents. These two steps prevent most frozen pipe calls.

## What should you do before an emergency plumber arrives for a burst pipe?

Shut off the main water valve right away, then open a low faucet to drain the lines. Turn off the water heater. Move belongings out of the water and call (833) 710-2588. Take photos for your insurer before cleanup. Do not use electrical outlets near standing water.

- Shut the main valve where the line enters the house.
- Open the lowest faucet to drain pressure.
- Turn the water heater to off or pilot.
- Switch off breakers for wet areas if safe.
- Call a plumber and your insurance company.

## How do you prevent frozen pipe repairs in Burien?

Most Burien winters are mild, but cold snaps do push temperatures into the teens. Insulate pipes in crawl spaces, garages, and outside walls. Disconnect hoses and cover outdoor faucets. Close crawl space vents during freezes. On the coldest nights, let a faucet on an outside wall drip.

- Wrap exposed pipes with foam insulation
- Install frost-free hose bibs on older homes
- Seal gaps where pipes pass through walls
- Keep the heat at 55°F or higher if you travel
- Know where your main shutoff is before it gets cold

Warning

Never thaw a frozen pipe with an open flame. Use a hair dryer and keep the faucet open so melting water can flow.

## How does pipe repair and whole-house repiping work?

For a single leak, the plumber cuts out the bad section and installs new pipe, then tests for leaks. For a repipe, we plan new routes, run new lines through crawl spaces and walls, connect each fixture, and pass inspection. Most repipes take 2 to 5 days, and you usually have water each night.

- Inspect. Check pipe type, condition, and pressure.
- Plan. Repair a section or repipe, with firm prices for each.
- Protect. Cover floors and work areas.
- Install. Replace pipe and connect fixtures.
- Test and inspect. Pressure test and pass the permit inspection.

## Which pipe materials need replacement in Burien homes?

Burien homes built before about 1960 often have galvanized steel supply pipe. Homes from the 1960s to 1990s usually have copper. Newer homes and recent remodels mostly use PEX. Some homes have a mix after partial updates. Knowing your pipe type helps us price the job on the phone.

| Pipe type | How to spot it | Typical lifespan |
| Galvanized steel | Dull gray, threaded joints, magnet sticks | 40 – 60 years |
| Copper | Reddish brown, soldered joints | 50 – 70 years |
| PEX | Red, blue, or white plastic tubing | 40+ years (expected) |
| CPVC | Cream-colored rigid plastic | 30 – 50 years |

## Should you repair a pipe or repipe the whole house?

Repair the pipe if it is your first leak and the rest of the plumbing is in good shape. Repipe if you have galvanized pipe, low pressure throughout, or repeated leaks. Repiping costs more up front, but it ends the cycle of leaks and water damage claims.

| Factor | Repair | Repipe |
| Pipe type | Copper or PEX in good shape | Galvanized or failing copper |
| Leaks in last 2 years | One | Two or more |
| Water pressure | Normal | Low throughout |
| Home age | Newer or updated | Original pre-1970 plumbing |

PEX is flexible, resists freezing better than copper, and costs less to install. Copper lasts a long time and some owners prefer it. Burien's soft water is gentle on both. We explain the tradeoffs and price both options so you can choose.

## Why hire pipe repair now instead of later?

Old pipes do not heal. Each leak risks water damage and mold, and galvanized pipe keeps narrowing until pressure drops to a trickle. Fixing the problem now protects your floors, walls, and insurance record. For burst pipes, every minute counts.

## Frequently asked questions

Short, direct answers to the questions we hear most on the phone. Do not see yours? Call and ask.

**Q: How do I know if I have galvanized pipes? **

Galvanized pipe is dull gray steel with threaded joints. Scratch it with a key. If it is silver-gray and a magnet sticks, it is galvanized. Copper is reddish brown, and PEX is colored plastic.

**Q: Is PEX good for repiping in Burien? **

Yes. PEX is approved by code, resists freezing, and works well with Burien's soft water. It is also quicker to install, which lowers labor cost.

**Q: How long does a whole-house repipe take? **

Most repipes take 2 to 5 days. We usually restore water at the end of each workday.

**Q: Can you repair a burst pipe at night? **

Yes. We repair burst pipes 24 hours a day. After-hours fees apply, and we tell you the fee on the phone.

**Q: Why is my water pressure low? **

In older homes, galvanized pipe rusts inside and narrows. Other causes are a failing pressure regulator, a partly closed valve, or a leak. A pressure test finds the cause.

**Q: Does repiping require opening walls? **

Some small openings are usually needed. In homes with crawl spaces, much of the pipe can be run underneath, which keeps wall openings small.

## What plumbing repairs do SeaTac homes need most?

SeaTac's most common plumbing problems are aging galvanized water lines in mid-century homes, root-clogged side sewers, worn-out water heaters, and shared drain stack clogs in apartments and condos. Wet winters also strain yard drains and sump pumps in low spots.

### Mid-century ramblers

Many SeaTac houses date from the 1950s and 1960s. If the plumbing has not been updated, the supply lines may be galvanized steel. That pipe rusts inside, so pressure drops and leaks start at threaded joints. The side sewer is often clay pipe, which lets roots in at the joints.

### Townhomes and newer builds

Newer homes near Angle Lake and along the light rail line mostly use PEX supply lines. Problems there tend to be fixture and valve failures, water heater issues, and clogs from construction debris in the first few years.

### Apartments and condos

In multi-unit buildings, one clog in a shared stack can back up into several units. Grease from kitchens is the top cause. Water heaters in these buildings also work hard and wear out faster.

### Airport-area remodels

Some homes near the airport have had noise insulation work, which often included new windows and doors. That work generally does not touch the plumbing, so the original pipes may still be in place even in homes that look updated.

## What plumbing repairs do White Center homes need most?

White Center's biggest plumbing problems come from age. Original galvanized supply pipe causes low pressure and leaks. Clay and cast iron sewer lines crack and fill with roots. Tight crawl spaces hide slow leaks. Small utility closets also make water heater swaps harder than in newer homes.

### Galvanized supply lines

If your White Center house still has its original plumbing, the water pipes are likely galvanized steel. After 70-plus years, the inside of that pipe is often packed with rust. You notice weak showers, brown water after a vacation, and leaks at threaded fittings. Patching one spot often moves the leak a few feet down the line.

### Old side sewers

Sewer lines from this era are usually clay or cast iron. Clay joints let roots in. Cast iron rusts and cracks. A camera inspection is the best way to see what you have before a backup forces the issue.

### Crawl spaces and small closets

Many homes here have shallow crawl spaces, which makes leaks hard to spot and repairs slower. Water heaters often sit in small closets where code items like seismic straps, drain pans, and venting need careful planning on replacement.

### Remodels and additions

Over the decades, many homes added a bathroom or moved a kitchen. Mixed pipe types and amateur connections show up often. We check those joints when we are working nearby.

## What plumbing repairs do Normandy Park homes need most?

Normandy Park homes deal most with root intrusion in sewer lines, long and sloped side sewers, yard water line leaks, and drainage issues on hillside lots. Mid-century homes may also have original galvanized supply pipe or older water heaters tucked in garages and crawl spaces.

### Roots and long runs

Large lots mean long side sewers, sometimes well over 100 feet from the house to the connection. More pipe means more joints, and more joints mean more places for roots from firs, cedars, and maples to get in. Repeat slow drains in the fall are a classic sign.

### Bluff and hillside homes

Homes on the slopes toward the Sound can have steep sewer runs, pumps, or unusual routing. Groundwater moving down the hill in winter can stress pipe bedding. We look at the full path with a camera before recommending any digging.

### Yard water lines

Long water service lines from the meter to the house can leak underground for months. Signs are a rising bill and soggy spots in dry weather. Leak detection finds the spot so only a small hole is needed.

### Septic or sewer

Most Normandy Park homes are on public sewer. If yours uses a septic system, tell us when you call. The signs of trouble and the right fix are different.

## What plumbing repairs do Seahurst homes need most?

### Daylight basements

Water moves downhill through the soil in the rainy season. Homes on the slope can see wet crawl spaces, busy sump pumps, and footing drains that clog with silt. Sewer lines on steep runs can also separate at joints over time.

The same tree canopy that makes Seahurst attractive sends roots into side sewers. Clay pipe joints are the usual entry point. A camera inspection shows how bad it is.

### Hidden leaks

A leak inside a finished basement ceiling or wall may only show as a small stain or a musty smell. Leak detection pinpoints it before you open drywall.

## Do Seahurst homes need sump pump repair or replacement?

Many do. Homes on the slope often rely on sump pumps and footing drains to keep lower levels dry in the rainy season. A pump that fails during a storm can flood a basement in hours. Test it in early fall, and replace pumps that are noisy, slow, or over 10 years old.

- Pour a bucket of water into the sump pit and watch the pump start.
- Check that water discharges well away from the foundation.
- Listen for grinding or rattling.
- Clear silt and debris from the pit.
- Consider a battery backup if power outages are common on your street.

If your pump runs nonstop in winter, groundwater may be higher than the pump can handle, or the check valve may have failed. Call and we will check it.

## Should you get a sewer inspection before buying in Seahurst?

Before buying in Seahurst, get a sewer camera inspection, check the age of the water heater, and look at how the lower level stays dry. Ask the seller about past backups, sump pump work, and pipe updates. These items are where the biggest surprise costs hide on sloped, older lots.

A camera inspection costs a few hundred dollars and can save thousands. We can usually schedule one within the inspection window. Call (833) 710-2588 to book.

## What plumbing repairs do Boulevard Park homes need most?

Boulevard Park's common problems are low water pressure and leaks from original galvanized pipe, root-packed clay side sewers, aging water heaters, and corroded shutoff valves that will not close in an emergency. Wet winters add yard drainage and crawl space moisture problems.

### Low pressure and rusty water

Galvanized steel pipe was standard when many Boulevard Park homes were built. Over 70 years, rust builds up inside until water barely gets through. If your shower is weak and your hot water runs brown after sitting, the pipes are a likely cause.

### Clay side sewers

Sewer lines from this era are often clay. Roots enter at the joints, and the line slowly fills. You may notice slow drains first, then gurgling, then a backup in the tub or a floor drain.

### Old shutoff valves

Original gate valves often seize. When a pipe bursts, the valve will not close, and the only option is the meter box at the street. Replacing the main shutoff with a modern ball valve is a cheap upgrade that pays off in an emergency.

### Crawl space moisture

Rainy months bring standing water to some crawl spaces. That speeds up corrosion on pipes and makes slow leaks harder to notice.

## How do you avoid frozen pipe repairs in Boulevard Park?

Insulate exposed pipes in the crawl space, close foundation vents, disconnect garden hoses, and cover outdoor faucets. On nights below about 20°F, let a faucet on an outside wall drip. If a pipe freezes, open the faucet, warm the pipe slowly with a hair dryer, and never use an open flame.

Older Boulevard Park homes often have pipes that run close to the foundation vents with little or no insulation. Those are the first to freeze. If you find a split pipe, shut off the main valve right away. When the pipe thaws, it will leak. Call (833) 710-2588 for frozen pipe repair , day or night.

## How can you check a plumber before you hire them in Washington?

In Washington you can look up any contractor on the Department of Labor & Industries "Verify a Contractor" tool. It shows registration, bond, insurance, and any violations. Plumbers working on your home also need a state plumber certificate. Ask for the contractor number on the call and check it.

We encourage every customer to do this, with us or with any plumber. It takes two minutes. Ask for the registration number, search it on the L&I website, and confirm the business name matches. This simple check protects you from unregistered contractors and helps if you ever need to file a claim against a bond.

Warning

Be wary of anyone who asks for full payment before starting a small repair.

## What should you have ready to get a fast quote?

Have your address, a short description of the problem, and when it started. If it is a water heater, have the brand, size, and fuel type from the label. Photos help too. If you rent, have your landlord's contact details. This helps us bring the right parts.

- Address and the best phone number to reach you
- What is happening and when it started
- Whether water is leaking now and if you shut it off
- Water heater label details: brand, gallons, gas or electric
- Age of the home, if you know it
- Photos you can text when asked
- Owner, landlord, or HOA contact if they approve the work

## When can you call a 24 hour plumber in Burien?

We are open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, including weekends and holidays. Daytime appointments on weekdays cost the least. Nights, weekends, and holidays carry an after-hours fee, which we tell you before booking so you can decide whether to wait.

| Time | Availability | Pricing |
| Weekdays, daytime | Scheduled and same-day visits | Standard rates |
| Evenings and nights | Emergency visits | After-hours fee |
| Weekends | Emergency and limited scheduled visits | After-hours fee |
| Holidays | Emergency visits | Holiday fee |

## What should you do before the emergency plumber arrives?

Shut off water to the problem area, stop using drains that are backing up, and clear a path to the fixture, water heater, or crawl space hatch. Move pets and valuables away. Take photos of any damage for insurance. These steps limit damage and help the plumber start faster.

- Shut it off. Use the fixture valve under the sink or toilet, or the main valve.
- Stop drain use. No flushing, showers, dishwasher, or laundry during a backup.
- Clear access. Move items from under sinks and around the water heater.
- Find the crawl space hatch or cleanout. Many Burien homes have both.
- Protect belongings. Lift rugs and boxes off wet floors.
- Document. Take photos and short videos for your insurer.

If you are not sure where your main valve is, we will help you find it while you are on the phone.

## Do you need emergency plumbing or a scheduled repair?

Book an emergency visit if water is spreading, sewage is backing up, you have no water, or your water heater is leaking. Book a scheduled visit for slow drains, dripping faucets, running toilets, or a water heater replacement you are planning. Scheduled visits cost less.

| Emergency: call now | Scheduled: book a time |
| Burst or spraying pipe | Dripping faucet |
| Sewage backup | One slow drain |
| Leaking water heater tank | Planned water heater upgrade |
| No water in the house | Running toilet |
| Frozen pipes | Repipe or sewer estimate |

Not sure which you have? Call and describe it. We will tell you honestly whether it can wait until morning.

## Can you get a second opinion on a plumbing quote?

Yes. If another company quoted a big job, like a sewer replacement or repipe, call us. Tell us what they found and what they quoted. We can review camera video if you have it, or inspect it ourselves, and give you our own price and recommendation.

A second opinion on a large job is smart and costs nothing on the phone.

Title: Privacy Policy
Summary: How we collect, use and protect call and website data on plumberburienwa.com. Questions about your privacy? Call (833) 710-2588.

# Privacy Policy

This policy explains what information we collect when you visit plumberburienwa.com or call Burien Plumbers, and how we use it.

## Information we collect

This website does not have forms and does not ask you to create an account. When you call us, we collect what you choose to share, such as your name, phone number, address, and details about your plumbing problem. We use it to schedule and complete your service.

### Call tracking

Our phone number is a call tracking number. Calls may be routed through a third-party provider that records the time, length, and source of the call, and calls may be recorded for quality and training. If a call is recorded, you will be told at the start of the call where required by law.

### Website data

Our hosting provider may log basic technical data, such as IP address, browser type, and pages visited, to keep the site secure and working. If we add analytics, it may use cookies to measure visits and clicks on phone links.

## How we use information

- To respond to your call and provide plumbing service
- To send quotes, invoices, and appointment updates
- To improve our service and website
- To meet legal and tax requirements

## Sharing

We do not sell your personal information. We share it only with service providers who help us run our business, such as call tracking, hosting, and payment processors, or when the law requires it.

## Your choices

You can ask us what information we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it where the law allows. Call (833) 710-2588 to make a request.

## Changes

We may update this policy. The date below shows the latest version.

# Terms of Use

These terms apply to your use of plumberburienwa.com. By using the site, you agree to them.

## Website information

The content on this site is general information about plumbing and our services. It is not a quote and not professional advice for your specific home. Prices shown are typical ranges for the Burien area and are not offers. Your actual price is given by the plumber after seeing the job.

## DIY information

Any do-it-yourself tips are provided for general guidance. Plumbing, gas, and electrical work can be dangerous. If you are unsure, stop and call a licensed professional. If you smell gas, leave the home and call your gas utility or 911.

## Service agreements

Plumbing work is governed by the written quote or work order you approve before work begins. That document controls the scope, price, and any terms for the job.

## Phone calls

Calls to our tracking number may be recorded and logged as described in our Privacy Policy .
